match.title: Live Class: Market Structure & Who Moves Price

json.title: Market structure — who really moves the price

guide.intro: You can read a chart. This week you find out who wrote it.
guide.outro: Structure is the record. Next week, the zones that make it.

steps.label: CORE CONCEPT
steps.heading: Price moves because someone has to fill an order

figure.caption: The reason a chart has a shape at all

body: A fund that wants two million shares cannot buy two million shares at one price. There is nobody on the other side offering that much at any single number. So the order gets worked — filled in pieces, at whatever prices there are sellers, over hours or days.

Every one of those fills moves the price a little further away from where they started. That is what you have been looking at for five belts: the track left behind by orders too large to fill in one go.

Market structure is how you read that track. It is not a pattern or an indicator. It is the sequence of highs and lows the market has actually made, in order, and it tells you which side has been getting filled.

steps.label: ON THE CHART
steps.heading: The four points that define structure
steps.intro: Every one of these is a point on a run of candles, not a part of one candle. Eleven real sessions in Tesla; tap each turn in order.
steps.prompt: Tap a marked turn on the chart — or a name below it — to read what that point is and why it counts.

marks.name: Swing low
marks.title: Swing low · 315.52 on 6 August
marks.body: A price the market fell to and then turned up from. It takes three sessions to see it: 5 August had to sell off, 6 August had to stop, and 7 August had to leave. One candle can never show you that. Until something closes below 315.52, this is still the last place buyers defended.

marks.name: Swing high
marks.title: Swing high · 336.20 on 11 August
marks.body: The top of the leg. Sellers stopped the advance here, and the two sessions either side both made lower highs — which is what turns a candle's high into a swing high. Not every high is one. This is the test.

marks.name: Higher low
marks.title: Higher low · 323.64 on 12 August
marks.body: The pullback after the swing high stopped at 323.64 — eight dollars above the 315.52 low that came before it. A low that is higher than the last low is the quiet half of an uptrend, and it is the reason you were still allowed to be long.

marks.name: Higher high
marks.title: Higher high · 351.26 on 14 August
marks.body: Price went straight through 336.20 and kept going, fifteen dollars past it. Now read the sequence out loud: higher low, higher high, higher low, higher high. That sentence is the whole of market structure — not a pattern, not an indicator, a sentence you can either say cleanly or not say at all.

steps.label: KEY DISTINCTION
steps.heading: A pullback, or a break of structure
steps.intro: Both look like price going the wrong way. Only one changes what you should do.

columns.title: Pullback — trend intact
points: Price dips but holds above the last swing low
The higher low is still higher
The order being filled is still being filled
You are looking for a place to join, not to leave

columns.title: Break — trend in question
points: Price CLOSES below the last swing low
The sequence of higher lows is broken
Whoever was being filled has stopped, or reversed
The prior read is void until new structure forms

steps.note: The test is a close, never a wick. A wick below the low is an attempt that failed; a close below it is the attempt succeeding. Every rule in this course rests on that one distinction.

steps.label: PROCESS
steps.heading: Mapping structure, in four moves
steps.intro: Do this before anything else on a chart. It takes under a minute once it is habit.

moves.title: Zoom out first
moves.body: Start on the daily, whatever you intend to trade. The biggest clock has the biggest crowd behind it, and the bigger crowd outranks the smaller one when they disagree.

moves.title: Mark the obvious swings only
moves.body: The turns you would point at from across the room. If you have to squint to justify a swing, it is not one — you are drawing your opinion, not the market's record.

moves.title: Read the sequence out loud
moves.body: Higher high, higher low, higher high — that is an uptrend and you say so. The moment you cannot say it cleanly, the market is in a range, and a range is a different game.

moves.title: Find the last decision point
moves.body: The most recent swing low in an uptrend, or swing high in a downtrend. That single level is what would have to give way for your read to be wrong. Everything else is commentary.

steps.closing: You now have a direction and the one price that would break it. That pair is the whole output of structure work, and it is what the next four weeks are built on.

steps.label: LIVE EXAMPLE
steps.heading: Tesla's wall, and the recovery under it
steps.intro: One session built the level. The fifteen sessions after it are what makes it a level at all.
steps.prompt: Tap the wall, the day that built it, and the three weeks the market spent underneath it.

marks.name: The wall
marks.title: The wall · 341.00 to 342.11
marks.body: On 23 July Tesla opened at 341.00 and got a dollar and eleven cents higher before it stopped. That dollar is the range across which a large seller was filled. It is drawn as a band and not a line because the fills happened at many prices, and price reacts to the band.

marks.name: The break
marks.title: 23 July closed at 319.69
marks.body: Twenty-one dollars below the open, and the session's low was 315.74 — so it did not close at the low; it closed $3.95 above it, in the bottom fifth of a twenty-six dollar range. That is still a break of structure. What makes it one is not where in the candle the close landed, but that the close landed below the swing low the uptrend had been standing on.

marks.name: Where it stopped
marks.title: The selling ended at 297.38 on 29 July
marks.body: Four sessions after the break, the fall stopped. Everything from here is a recovery, and every dollar of it happened underneath a ceiling that was built in a single morning.

marks.name: Three weeks below
marks.title: Fourteen sessions, none of them back at the wall
marks.body: From 24 July to 12 August the closest Tesla came to 341.00 was 336.20, on 11 August — still $4.80 short. Nobody had to remember what happened on 23 July. The orders left resting in that band did the remembering.

marks.name: The return
marks.title: 13 August · 341.64, and no further
marks.body: Three weeks later price finally reached the wall — and stopped 47 cents under its top at 342.11, closing back down at 339.96. That is what a level is: not a line on a screen, but a queue of resting orders that holds until the queue is used up.

steps.label: DEEPER INSIGHT
steps.heading: Why a level is a level
body: A price becomes important because of what happened there, not because of the number. At 341 a large seller was filled. That is a fact about supply, and it does not evaporate when the day ends.

It matters twice. Anyone who sold there and was right will sell there again. And anyone who bought just under it and got hurt will take the first chance to get out at break-even — which is more selling, at the same price, for a different reason.
So a level is not a line on your screen. It is a queue of resting orders, and it holds until that queue is used up. When you hear that price is 'respecting' a level, this is the whole mechanism.
Read a chart as a map of where the orders are, and it stops being a picture of the past.

steps.label: KNOWLEDGE CHECK
steps.question: In an uptrend, price wicks below the last swing low and closes back above it. What has happened to the structure?
options: The uptrend is broken — a new low was made
The uptrend is intact — the low held on a closing basis
Nothing can be said until the next daily candle
The trend becomes a range automatically
steps.explanation: A wick is an attempt; a close is a result. Price reached below the low and was rejected, which is the low doing its job.

wrongFeedback.text: A low is broken by a CLOSE below it, not by a wick reaching under it. The wick is the attempt failing.
The candle in question has already closed — that is the information. Waiting for another one is a different decision.
A trend becomes a range when the sequence of higher highs and higher lows stops, which has not happened here.

steps.reinforce: Closes, never wicks. This single rule decides more calls than anything else in the course.

steps.label: KNOWLEDGE CHECK
steps.question: The daily says uptrend and the five-minute says downtrend. Which one sets your direction?
options: The five-minute — it is the most recent information
The daily — the bigger clock carries the bigger crowd
Neither, they cancel out and you stand aside
Whichever agrees with your existing position
steps.explanation: A daily candle is every large participant voting across a full session; a five-minute candle is a few thousand fast traders. The big clock sets direction, the small clock sets timing.

wrongFeedback.text: Most recent is not the same as most important. The five-minute is where you time an entry, not where you decide which way to face.
They do not cancel. A pullback on a small clock inside an uptrend on a big one is the most ordinary thing on a chart — and often the opportunity.
That is the position talking, not the chart. The ladder is read top-down regardless of what you already hold.

steps.reinforce: Top-down, every time. Big clocks set direction, small clocks set timing.

steps.label: WRAP UP
steps.heading: Key takeaways
points: Price moves because orders too large to fill at one price get worked through the book. The chart is the track they leave.
Structure is the sequence of swing highs and lows, read in order — not a pattern and not an indicator.
A pullback holds the last swing; a break closes through it. The test is always a close, never a wick.
A level matters because of the orders filled there, and because of the traders trapped just under it.
The output of structure work is two things: a direction, and the one price that would prove it wrong.
steps.closing: Next: the zones those big orders were filled in, and why price keeps coming back to them.

match.title: Drill: Map the Structure on 3 Charts

json.title: Drill — map the structure on three charts

guide.intro: Three charts. Call the structure before you read the answer.

steps.label: PROCESS
steps.heading: How this drill is graded
body: Three real charts, one question each. The chart is on the screen before the options are — read it, decide, then choose. A call you revise after seeing the options is not a call.
You are not being asked to predict anything. You are being asked to say what the market has already done, which is the only thing structure can tell you.

steps.label: EXERCISE
steps.question: Tesla, daily. It bottomed at 297.38 on 29 July, made a higher low at 315.52, ran to 336.20, and has just pulled back to 323.64. What is the structure?

options.label: Uptrend — higher highs and higher lows
Range — no sequence you can say cleanly

reveal.headline: Uptrend, and it kept going
reveal.body:
Lows 297.38 → 315.52 → 323.64. Highs 329.57 → 333.73 → 336.20. Both sequences rising, so you can say it out loud without squinting — and that is the whole test.

The two sessions after the one you were shown took it to 341.64 and then 351.26. The structure was already telling you which way to lean before either of them printed.

marks.name: Low 1
marks.title: Low 1
marks.body: 297.38 on 29 July.

marks.name: High 1
marks.title: High 1
marks.body: 329.57 on 4 August.

marks.name: Low 2
marks.title: Low 2
marks.body: 315.52 on 6 August.

marks.name: High 2
marks.title: High 2
marks.body: 336.20 on 11 August.

marks.name: Low 3
marks.title: Low 3
marks.body: 323.64 on 12 August — the pullback you are being asked about.

steps.label: EXERCISE
steps.question: Tesla, five-minute. Four candles have turned within sixty-six cents of 321.05. The 10:00 candle trades down to 320.79 and closes at 323.12. Has that low broken?

options.label: Intact — the close came back above it

reveal.headline: Intact — and this is the whole rule
reveal.body:
The trade to 320.79 is the attempt. The close at 323.12 is the result, and it is $2.07 back above the level. A wick through is an attempt that failed; a close through is the attempt succeeding.

Anyone who called this broken sold the low of the pullback, which is exactly what the wick was there to collect. Tesla's lowest print for the rest of that session was 322.77 and it closed the day at 327.38.

marks.name: The low
marks.title: The swing low · 321.05
marks.body: Four candles turned between 321.05 and 321.71 — that flat underside is the level being tested.

marks.name: The attempt
marks.title: Traded to 320.79
marks.body: Twenty-six cents under the low. That is the attempt.

marks.name: The close
marks.title: Closed at 323.12
marks.body: Two dollars and seven cents back above the low. That is the result.

marks.name: After
marks.title: The next half hour
marks.body: It never went back down there.

steps.label: EXERCISE
steps.question: Tesla, daily. It has been holding above 369 all week. On 23 July it opens at 341.00, tops at 342.11 and closes at 319.69. What is the read the next morning?

options.label: Uptrend continues, this was a pullback
Structure is broken; 341–342 is now a ceiling above
Buy it, that is a discount

reveal.headline: Broken — and the wall is now overhead
reveal.body:
A close fifty dollars below the last swing low is a break of structure, whatever the rest of the candle did. Tesla did not close at its low that day — the low was 315.74 and it recovered $3.95 into the bell — and it does not matter. The close was through the level, and that is the test.

Everything Tesla did for the next three weeks happened underneath 341–342. It bottomed at 297.38 on 29 July and it took until 13 August to get back within a dollar of the wall. Real session, real numbers.

marks.name: The last low
marks.title: The last swing low · 369.43
marks.body: The floor the trend had been standing on, made on 20 July.

marks.name: The wall
marks.title: 341.00 to 342.11
marks.body: Where 23 July opened and stopped. Twenty-seven dollars below the low it had just broken.

marks.name: The close
marks.title: Closed 319.69
marks.body: Fifty dollars below the last swing low, in one session.

marks.name: After
marks.title: What followed
marks.body: Six more sessions down to 297.38 on 29 July.

marks.name: The bottom
marks.body: Where the selling finally stopped.

steps.label: WRAP UP
steps.heading: What the drill was testing
points: Say the sequence out loud. If you cannot, it is a range, not a trend you are being clever about.
Wick below, close above: the level held. That is not a technicality, it is the level working.
A break of structure changes the map — the broken level becomes the ceiling you now trade beneath.
steps.closing: Three for three, or go back to the class and re-read the four moves. There is no shame in the second option and a lot of cost in skipping it.
